chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Yazeed who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who guaranteed for another man with a guarantee, then reconciled upon it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not entitled to anything except that which he had reconciled upon.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on the amount a guarantor can claim from the debtor after settling the debt?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *sulh* (amicable settlement) in debt recovery, ruling that a guarator who settles a debt with the creditor is entitled to recover only the actual amount paid, preventing unjust enrichment or arbitrary claims against the debtor. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on fairness and the binding nature of mutual agreement in financial transactions, ensuring that the guarantor does not profit from the settlement process. It reflects the broader Islamic legal ethic of *adl* (justice) in contractual obligations.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who guarantees upon a man with a guarantee, then reconciles upon it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not for him (an amount) except that which he had reconciled upon’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ’Isa, from Muhammad ibn ’Isa from ibn Bukayr from ’Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following:

"I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who has bailed out another man and has reached a settlement with him.’ He (the Imam) said, ’He can only have the actual amount the man owes to him.”’
